skills.name: What a solution is

steps.a: check an ordered pair in both equations

skills.wrong_turn: A pair that works in one equation isn't a solution. It must satisfy every equation in the system.
skills.rule: A solution of a system is an ordered pair that makes every equation true.

skills.name: Solve by graphing
skills.wrong_turn: A graph only estimates. If lines cross near (1.3, 2.7), check it in the equations before calling it the answer.
skills.rule: Graph both lines; the intersection point is the solution.

skills.name: Substitution
skills.wrong_turn: Substitute into the other equation, not back into the one you rearranged, or you'll get 0 = 0 and learn nothing.
skills.rule: Solve one equation for a variable, substitute into the other, solve, then back-substitute.

skills.name: Elimination
skills.wrong_turn: When subtracting equations, subtract every term: (3x + 2y) − (x − 2y) is 2x + 4y, not 2x.
skills.rule: Add or subtract the equations so one variable cancels.

skills.name: Elimination with multiplying
skills.wrong_turn: Multiply the constant too: 2x + 3y = 12 times 2 is 4x + 6y = 24, not 4x + 6y = 12.
skills.rule: Multiply one or both equations so a variable has opposite coefficients, then add.

skills.name: Choosing a method
skills.wrong_turn: Substitution with fractions isn't wrong, just messy. If no coefficient is 1, elimination usually saves mistakes.
skills.rule: Graph to see, substitute when a variable is alone, eliminate when coefficients line up.

skills.name: No or infinite solutions
skills.wrong_turn: Getting 0 = 0 doesn't mean the solution is (0, 0). It means every point on the line is a solution.
skills.rule: Parallel lines: no solution. The same line: infinitely many solutions.

skills.name: Systems word problems
skills.wrong_turn: Keep the variables meaningful: if a counts adult tickets, 8a is dollars, and a + k counts tickets. Don't add dollars to tickets.
skills.rule: Name two variables, write two equations, solve, and answer in words.

skills.name: Mixture problems
skills.wrong_turn: Percentages don't add: mixing 20% and 50% acid never makes 70%. The result is between 20% and 50%.
skills.rule: One equation for total amount, one for total pure substance or value.

skills.name: Rate & distance systems
skills.wrong_turn: The trip against the current uses b − c, not c − b. The boat must still move forward, so b is bigger.
skills.rule: Downstream speed b+c, upstream speed b−c, and distance = rate × time.

skills.name: Systems of inequalities

steps.d: write the system from a graph

skills.wrong_turn: The solution is where all the shading overlaps, not everywhere any shading appears.
skills.rule: Graph each inequality; the solution is the overlap of the shaded regions.

skills.name: Linear programming basics
skills.wrong_turn: The best point isn't the one farthest from the origin. Check the objective at every vertex.
skills.rule: The maximum or minimum of a linear objective over the feasible region occurs at a vertex.

skills.name: Three-variable systems
skills.wrong_turn: Eliminate the same variable from both pairs. Removing z from one pair and x from another leaves three unknowns again.
skills.rule: Eliminate one variable twice to get a two-variable system, solve it, then back-substitute.

skills.name: Linear–quadratic systems

steps.a: sketch a line and a parabola

skills.wrong_turn: Each x needs its own y. For x = 2 and x = −1 there are two points, not one point (2, −1).
skills.rule: Substitute the line into the quadratic and solve; expect 0, 1 or 2 solutions.

skills.name: Matrices for systems
skills.wrong_turn: Change a whole row at a time. R2 − 3R1 must hit the constant too: 1 − 3·5 = −14.
skills.rule: Row-reduce the augmented matrix [A∣𝐛] to echelon form, then back-substitute.
